before.answer:
SOP-11: Report every staff injury, including needle-stick injuries, to your Clinic Manager within 24 hours of the incident by completing the Incident Report form (IR-01). The Clinic Manager forwards the form to the Facilities and Safety Manager within 48 hours.
SOP-04: Report the injury to the Occupational Health Officer by phone within 2 hours of the incident, and complete the Sharps Injury Form (OH-05) before the end of the same shift. The 2-hour window exists because PEP for HIV is most effective when started within 2 hours and should not be started later than 72 hours.
before.question: Within how many hours must a needle-stick injury be reported?
before.expected: SOP-04 v3.0 (2026) says report to Occupational Health within 2 hours; SOP-11 v1.2 (2023) says report to Clinic Manager within 24 hours on IR-01. A good answer surfaces both, notes SOP-04 is newer and more specific, and recommends the 2-hour rule while flagging the conflict.

before.answer:
SOP-06: Record the refrigerator temperature twice daily, at clinic opening and at clinic closing, in the Cold Chain Log (CC-01). Record the minimum and maximum temperatures from the data logger at the same time.
SOP-09: Insulin, some eye drops and vaccines stocked by the pharmacy are kept in the pharmacy refrigerator at 2 to 8 degrees Celsius. Record the refrigerator temperature once daily at clinic opening in the pharmacy log (PH-03).
before.question: How often should the vaccine refrigerator temperature be recorded?
before.expected: SOP-06 says twice daily (opening and closing) for the vaccine fridge; SOP-09 says once daily for the pharmacy fridge, which also stores some vaccines. A good answer notes the difference and recommends the stricter twice-daily rule for any fridge holding vaccines.

after_update.answer: SOP-02: A patient arriving more than 15 minutes late is moved to the next free slot or the walk-in queue. Mark no-shows in the CMS at the end of the session.
citations: SOP-02 v2.4, section 4 (No-shows and late arrivals), page 1
after_update.question: What percentage of slots should be kept free for walk-ins?
after_update.expected: 25% until 9:00 AM (SOP-02 v2.4). Answering 20% means stale chunks or a stale cache.

after_update.answer: SOP-08: Front-desk staff can approve refunds up to Rs 1,500 for billing errors. Refunds between Rs 1,500 and Rs 10,000 need Clinic Manager approval.
after_update.question: Up to what amount can front-desk staff approve a refund?
after_update.expected: Rs 1,500 (SOP-08 v2.1). Rs 1,000 means stale data.

after_update.answer:
SOP-11: Report every staff injury to your Clinic Manager within 24 hours of the incident by completing the Incident Report form (IR-01). Exception: needle-stick and sharps injuries must first be reported to the Occupational Health Officer within 2 hours, as set out in SOP-04.
SOP-04: Report the injury to the Occupational Health Officer by phone within 2 hours of the incident, and complete the Sharps Injury Form (OH-05) before the end of the same shift. The 2-hour window exists because PEP for HIV is most effective when started within 2 hours and should not be started later than 72 hours.
after_update.question: Within how many hours must a needle-stick injury be reported?
after_update.expected: Within 2 hours to Occupational Health (SOP-04), and IR-01 within 24 hours (SOP-11 v2.0). There is no longer a conflict; reporting one means the old SOP-11 v1.2 chunks were not removed.
